title: Lamb Madras
subtitle: Hot, sour curry-house lamb curry
excerpt: A fiery curry-house staple: lamb cooked in a tomato-based sauce with plenty of chilli and a sharp hit of tamarind. This is a robust, deeply coloured curry with more heat than a tikka masala and a tartness that cuts through the richness of the meat.

recipe.sourceNotes: Madras curry is a British-Indian restaurant creation named loosely after the city of Madras (now Chennai), though it bears little resemblance to any dish from that region of south India. It became one of the most popular curry-house orders in Britain by the 1970s: hotter than a standard curry, sharper from the addition of tamarind or tomato, typically ordered by those who liked heat alongside korma and tikka masala on the menu. It is defined by its British-Indian restaurant context, not by a traditional Indian recipe.

recipeTools.notes: Wide heavy pan for the curry.

content.text: A madras needs time to develop its depth: the base sauce should cook until the oil starts to separate before the lamb goes in, and then the whole thing needs a long, slow simmer. The tamarind provides the signature sourness. Adjust the chilli level to your tolerance: two to three teaspoons of chilli powder gives a proper curry-house level of heat.

Heat the oil in a large heavy pan over medium heat. Add the cardamom, cinnamon, and bay leaves. Cook for 1 minute. Add the onion and cook for 15 minutes until deep golden, stirring often. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 3 minutes.

Add the chilli powder, coriander, cumin, turmeric, and paprika. Stir for 2 minutes over the heat. Add the tinned tomatoes and tamarind paste. Cook, stirring often, for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens and the oil begins to separate at the edges.

Add the lamb pieces and salt. Stir to coat in the sauce. Add 200 ml water. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 45 minutes until the lamb is very tender. Check and stir every 15 minutes, adding a splash more water if it sticks.

Remove the lid and simmer for 10 more minutes to thicken the sauce. Add the garam masala and stir through. Remove the cinnamon stick and cardamom pods. Scatter with fresh coriander and serve with basmati rice or naan.
